$handoff.title: GFA ATAK — Threaded Messaging
$handoff.scope: The threaded messaging engine ONLY: store, transport, template schema, channels, tags, subscriptions. Tasking rides on this (a task is a thread) but its templates and transition rules are a separate handoff.
outOfScope: App framework / shell / device model / render surfaces
BFT — already exists as the user's own working scripts
Notification presentation — the mission framework already has a notification system; call the seam only
Video feeds — vanilla Arma 3 custom info panels
EW link-state source — comes from the user's existing ew-zones addon
supersedes: cTab / cTAB Advanced as a dependency — dropped entirely; no compat layer, no ctab_fnc_registerMessageTemplate
Any message 'priority' enum — replaced by tags
Any To/box addressing model — replaced by post-to-channel + tags

principles: Server is the single authority. Every message body exists once, on the server.
Clients hold a disposable cache. If it is lost or stale, refetch. Nothing on a client is authoritative.
Never publicVariable the store. Never store messages on objects. Both replicate payloads to every machine for the whole mission.
A thread is the unit of everything — a message, a task, a conversation, an archive entry.
Templates are data, never hardcoded in the UI layer.
Sort messages by seq, never by time. Two replies in one frame otherwise order arbitrarily.
Presentation is not this system's job. Notifications go through one seam.
Build the transport first, with no UI. If that is not solid, nothing above it will be.

message.fromUid: string — taken from the caller server-side, NEVER from the client payload
message.tags: array of string — alert tags and audience tags combined
message.transition: enum threadStatus|null — state this message caused

thread.channelId: string — the channel it was posted in
thread.subject: string — derived from root template subjectFormat, never typed by a user
thread.participants: array of uid — grows when audience tags pull people in
thread.followers: array of uid — explicit per-thread follow, overrides channel subscription

anchor.marker: string|null — soft reference only; markers get moved and deleted
anchor.label: string snapshot of marker text

thread.messages: array of messageId in seq order

channel.id: string — C2 | C2.reports | FIRES | FIRES.cas | SQUAD:<groupId>
channel.parent: string|null — one level of nesting only

members.roles: array of role variable names, e.g. isJFO
members.group: string|null — engine group id, for squad channels

channel.derived: bool — squad channels are created on demand from the engine group, not declared

indexEntry.description: What a client receives on join. No message bodies.
indexEntry.subject: string

channels.nesting: One level. A sub-channel inherits its parent's retention and forwardToAlive unless overridden.

derivedSquad.membership: the engine group, resolved at delivery time — NOT cached on the channel
derivedSquad.note: Membership must resolve at delivery so mid-mission group reassignment works. Old-squad history stays readable in the archive but stops notifying.

channels.membershipNote: Membership is a union of role flags, explicit uids, and group. Overlaps are intentional (rotary crews sit in FIRES.trans and MEDICAL.medevac) — dedupe recipients before notifying.

tags.description: Tags do two jobs. Both live in the same array; the resolver treats them differently.

alert.source: derived from the template and the channel — NEVER self-declared by the sender
alert.reason: If senders can declare FLASH, everything is FLASH by mission three.

behaviour.FLASH: forces the surface open, sound, ignores mute

audience.values: channel ids, squad names, role names, or a uid
effect: adds those players to thread.participants — this IS a permission grant, they can reply
notifies them regardless of channel subscription
thread stays in its posted channel; it is NOT duplicated
audience.example: Post a TASKING in C2 tagged NOMAD. Thread lives in C2 and is visible to C2 members. Nomad's members are added as participants, notified, and can WILCO — and that WILCO is visible to C2.

resolution.level: max(alert tag levels on the message)
resolution.escalation: +1 level if the recipient is an addressee, a claimant, or matched by an audience tag
resolution.muteOverride: FLASH and audience-tag matches ignore mute; nothing else does

subscriptions.surface: a settings page, one row per channel the player is a member of
rules: Only channels the player is a member of appear. Subscription is not access.
The squad row is shown but locked to ALERT.
Defaults: own squad and role channels ALERT, parent channels BADGE, everything else MUTE — sensible enough that nobody has to visit the page.
Per-thread follow/unfollow lives in the thread view, not settings, and overrides the channel level either way.

storage.client: profileNamespace — a personal preference that should persist across missions
storage.server: client sends prefs on join; server caches for the session because notification filtering happens at delivery

templateSchema.origin: Superset of the PLANOPS Maps export format (maps-beta.plan-ops.fr). The lines[]/fields[] nesting maps onto doctrinal line numbering — keep it.
templateSchema.conversion: The user's existing templates are reference data, not code. Read field layouts out of them and re-express in this schema. One mechanical pass.
gapsInSourceFormat: No field IDs — generate keys from position (L3.A), never from labels, which get edited
No required flags — add them; a MEDEVAC with no grid is useless
No exclusive-choice grouping — checkbox sets like security N/P/E/X are single-choice in doctrine
No autofill — this is the entire adoption story, see autoFill below
Lines with empty fields[] are section headers; the renderer must not choke on them

template.id: string — stable key; do NOT use the PLANOPS uid
template.title: string
template.tags: array of string — alert tags this template always carries
template.replyableWith: array of templateId — drives which reply buttons the thread shows

field.key: string — generated from position, stable across label edits
field.label: string
field.allowManual: bool, default TRUE — never leave a grid field dropdown-only; the failure case is a target nobody has marked yet

markerPicker.why: Typing grids by hand is where these systems lose people.
markerPicker.build: on composer open, not per frame
filters: exclude by marker-name prefix — a mission setting; the user's own BFT prefix and ALiVE's go in it once
markerPicker.label: markerText if non-empty, else marker name; plus grid and range/bearing from sender
markerPicker.sort: distance ascending — this makes the dropdown a de-facto nearest-contacts list
markerPicker.payload: store the RESOLVED position plus a label snapshot. Marker name is a soft reference only. A message is a record of what was reported at the time and must not change when a marker moves.
markerPicker.reverse: also offer create-marker-from-received-field, so an inbound report can be dropped on the map in one click

templateExamples.title: WILCO
templateExamples.note: Zero fields. Sendable from a keybind without opening any UI.

templateExamples.title: CANTCO
templateExamples.note: Reason is required. Declining silently is how tasks get lost.

templateExamples.title: Message
templateExamples.note: Build this one first. It is most of the real traffic and it unblocks the transport spike.

threadSet.note: Minimum viable set. Everything else is added when someone asks.
threadSet.volume: SPOTREP and FREETEXT will be ~70% of traffic. Make those fast; the rare ones can be clunky.

cfgRemoteExec.note: Declare these or messaging silently fails on a locked-down server.

validates: sender is a member of channelId
sender is a thread participant when threadId is set
effects: assign id, seq, sentTime; fromUid from the caller, not the payload
create thread on root, else append
resolve audience tags to uids; merge into thread.participants
push to online recipients; forward to ALiVE if reportable and channel.forwardToAlive

srvRequestIndex.returns: array of indexEntry — index ONLY, no bodies. Keeps JIP cost flat regardless of traffic volume.

effects: update readBy — do NOT broadcast read receipts
set claimedBy if unclaimed; post a system message into the thread
srvClaim.why: Two pilots launching for the same MEDEVAC is the failure this prevents.

effects: resolve alert level and call the notify seam

notifySeam.name: GFA_fnc_notify
notifySeam.rule: Core NEVER calls the mission's notification API directly. One file to change if that system changes.
notifySeam.note: A TIC with four replies in five seconds needs throttling, and collapsing to '3 new in FIRES' is a messaging decision, not a display one.

rules: never store on objects or the device item
convert HashMaps to arrays before crossing the network and rebuild with createHashMapFromArray — HashMap remoteExec serialization is unverified and not worth finding out mid-op
keep the store on the server proper, not a headless client — HCs get restarted

persistence.scope: channels with retention=archive only; personal/ephemeral threads are not persisted
persistence.format: nested arrays only — no HashMaps in the namespace
caveats: tied to the host machine's .vars.Arma3Profile; does not follow a host change unless the file is copied
no query layer — the whole archive loads into memory
if it outgrows this: iniDBI2 (archives become readable out-of-game for AAR) or ALiVE persistence
persistence.why: An archive that dies at mission end is not an archive. This is in scope for v1 because named channels are archives.

linkState.source: the user's existing ew-zones addon; evaluated SERVER-side, not client — a client flag is trivially wrong when someone walks out of a zone mid-send
linkState.principle: Degrade, do not disable. A frozen map with a timestamp is better play than a blank screen.
linkState.lpiException: Low-bandwidth traffic (text and templates) still passes in DENIED on LPI-capable radios; feeds and BFT do not. Mirrors the existing voice-jamming exemption.

failureCases: recipient disconnects mid-send — server stores it, delivers on reconnect by uid
double submit — disable the send control client-side AND dedupe on draftNonce server-side
sender dies or goes unconscious while composing — block send; a dead man filing his own MEDEVAC is a strange artifact
thread with zero online participants — still valid, just idle; do not garbage-collect on participant count
marker referenced by a thread gets deleted — anchor.pos still holds; never re-resolve from marker name
player changes engine group mid-mission — squad channel membership must resolve at delivery time

buildOrder.what: Transport only. Store, srvSubmit, cltReceive, FREETEXT template hardcoded, hint the output. No UI at all.
buildOrder.why: Half a day, and it de-risks the whole stack. Building the form renderer first is how you end up with a beautiful composer that cannot send anything.

buildOrder.what: Index + thread view UI. Still FREETEXT only.
Template engine — schema loader and runtime form renderer. Convert MEDEVAC first, then CAS 9-line.
buildOrder.why: If the schema survives a second real template unchanged, it is probably right.

buildOrder.what: Pickers and autofill — marker dropdown, map click, callsign, TFAR frequency.
buildOrder.why: This is the adoption story, not polish.

buildOrder.what: Channels, subscriptions settings page, claim, archive persistence.
Tags, alert resolution, notify seam, rate limiting.
ALiVE C2ISTAR ingest, thread map anchors, EW link-state degradation.

openQuestions.q: Reply defaults to the channel or to the sender?
openQuestions.recommendation: channel, with an explicit reply-to-sender option. Defaulting to sender leaves archives full of half-conversations, which is the worst outcome for an AAR record.

openQuestions.q: Do HashMaps survive remoteExec serialization intact?
openQuestions.status: unverified — this spec assumes not and converts to arrays

openQuestions.q: Exact TFAR accessor for the active radio's frequency
openQuestions.status: TFAR_fnc_activeSwRadio / activeLrRadio are confirmed; the settings getter for frequency is not. Check the TFAR wiki rather than guessing.

openQuestions.q: Does a CustomDisplayComponent attach to an infantry unit at all?
openQuestions.status: unverified, ~20 min editor test. Gates whether an info-panel surface can carry an unread badge. The dialog path works regardless, so it does not block this handoff.

relatedHandoffsNeeded: Tasking — X-line tasking templates and their transition rules (rides on this system; a task IS a thread)
App framework and devices — shell, app contract hooks, device capability table, surface gating, widget slots, core map draw dispatcher
